author: Inspection team (fictional)
statement: The east culvert can carry the flow expected in the September planning scenario.
context: Fictional Brookside association; east culvert; a planning exercise for September 2026, not a real flood forecast.
assumptions: The inlet remains clear of debris.
The historical cross-section still represents the culvert.

author: Residents group (fictional)
statement: The north access route can remain open during a one-day culvert inspection.
context: Fictional Brookside association; foot access for eight households during a proposed inspection.
assumptions: Inspection equipment stays within the marked work area.
limitations: Emergency access has not been assessed.

author: Inspection team (fictional)
summary: The fictional design plan shows capacity above the assumed planning flow.
method: Compare a design drawing with the stated planning scenario; no field calibration.
limitations: The design drawing predates recent debris accumulation.

author: Residents group (fictional)
summary: The invented resident log describes backed-up water and debris at the inlet.
method: Structured recollection from two observers after the fictional rainfall exercise.
limitations: The observations may share the same underlying event.

author: Access coordinator (fictional)
summary: A fictional route walk found space for a temporary pedestrian corridor.
method: Walk the proposed path using the equipment footprint on the plan.
limitations: Does not establish accessibility for every resident.

author: Design reviewer (fictional)
rationale: The design comparison supports the capacity claim under the clear-inlet assumption; it does not establish current inlet condition.

author: Resident reviewer (fictional)
rationale: Observed backup challenges the clear-inlet assumption. The design alone is insufficient for a current capacity conclusion.

author: Access reviewer (fictional)
rationale: The route appears feasible, but residents with mobility constraints have not yet reviewed it.

author: Planning group (fictional)
action: Inspect and document the inlet before any capacity-dependent work is approved.
rationale: The conflicting accounts can be narrowed by checking the condition on which the drawing-based estimate depends.
alternatives: Accept the design estimate without inspection.
Commission a full model before inspecting.
dissent: The resident reviewer objects to describing the culvert as currently adequate.
success_criteria: Record inlet condition, photographs and measurements sufficient to decide whether a separate capacity study is needed.
stop_condition: Stop the inspection if access or weather makes the work unsafe; arrange a qualified inspection.

author: Planning group (fictional)
action: Ask affected residents to review the temporary access arrangement before setting an inspection date.
rationale: A route walk cannot establish that the arrangement works for all affected residents.
alternatives: Close the route for the day.
dissent: The route must not be treated as accessible until affected residents have responded.
success_criteria: Record responses from the affected households and document any unresolved access needs.
stop_condition: Do not schedule a closure while an affected household lacks an agreed access arrangement.

author: Inspection coordinator (fictional)
observation: In the fictional exercise the inlet was partly blocked. The inspection recorded its condition but could not establish hydraulic capacity.
next_action: Request a qualified capacity assessment using the current inlet condition; keep the original disagreement attached.
